design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (fbn_storage_inventory_reimbursements), revision 2. Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1): {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 5]}. Root inbound-shortage approval takes 6 factors, the claim correction 4, the warehouse-damage approval 5.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The seller asks only for his inbound-shortage claim to be decided. The approval rule carries two prerequisite sentences: the result is not fixed until the units claimed equal the claimable shortage of the line, and a shortage case is decided only after no earlier warehouse-damage case of the same SKU still stands submitted. The agent must find the earlier damage case on the same SKU, decide it with its own five-factor policy (inside its damage claim span), compute the claimable shortage (same-cost netting across the shipment, over-receipt carry-forward, receiving tolerance) and hand the correction to the seller, and only then compute the approval, whose inbound verification holdback reads the case history that the damage decision just changed.

2. SCOPE. Task 0 owns the lost-in-warehouse pair. Task 1 claims fulfill_ext_shortage_claim_units (amend_inbound_shortage_claim_fdee09ae, owner user), fulfill_ext_damaged_case_approval (approve_damaged_inventory_case_556f0f6d, owner agent) and fulfill_ext_shortage_case_approval (approve_inbound_shortage_case_dfebd527, owner agent). All five policies are covered across the two tasks with disjoint scopes.

3. DESIGN CONSTRAINT. FBN money events trigger payout writes, so scored writes are the unit counts on fulfill_cases; Northloop's reimbursement run pays separately and nothing in the tree waits for it. Each tool takes the six source keys bound by the inherited no_double_reimbursement gate.

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD (fan-out). Root fulfill_ext_shortage_case_approval.
 Edge A: -> fulfill_ext_shortage_claim_units, value_input, gate inbound_claimed, form state. Sentence: "The units approved on an inbound shortage case are not fixed until the units claimed on that case equal the claimable shortage of its shipment line." Opening: the shortage case claims 38; the claimable shortage is 26. Only the seller's correction writes the units claimed of an open shortage case. Skip run: 25 instead of 23.
 Edge B: -> fulfill_ext_damaged_case_approval, value_input, gate inbound_approved, form state. Sentence: "An inbound shortage case is decided only after no warehouse-damage case of the same SKU opened before it still stands submitted." Opening: the damage case of WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR opened 2026-09-03 is submitted, before the shortage case of 2026-09-14. Only the damage approval changes that case's status. Value effect: approving it raises the approved reimbursement-case count inside 12 months from 2 to 3, moving the seller to the waived inbound verification holdback. Skip run: 22 instead of 23.
 Four-point test on both: ordering connective (not until / only after); record-visible state; no tool, id or code token; scope exactly the case's own line / earlier damage cases of the same SKU. Order between the prerequisites: different cases, neither policy reads the other's case; replaying the correction first gives the same root value 23 and the same terminal rows.

5. FACTOR CARD - damage approval (5 factors: 4 parameter, 1 method; standard result 8, gold 22). damage_allowance_method (method, multi-source: enrollment program + standing level rows, cross standing): Core AND Top Rated -> 1 x 2 damage adjustments in 6 months = 2 (standard floor(465 x 0.002) = 0) -> 23; damage_allowance_cap (parameter): 52 months -> 1 (standard 4) -> 21; damage_compliance_holdback (parameter, cross standing): 8 points -> 3 (standard 1) -> 23; damage_approval_limit (parameter, cross selling): Basic Store -> 20 (standard 8) -> 11; damage_limit_uplift (parameter): opened 36 days ago -> 3 (standard 0) -> 20. The starting units are the units claimed limited to the damage adjustments inside the 2-month damage claim span (26 = 10 + 16); near-miss: the 2026-02-15 damage adjustment (5 units) is outside both spans and was reimbursed automatically.

6. FACTOR CARD - claim correction (4 factors: 3 parameter, 1 method; standard result 31, gold 26): netting_scope (method, multi-source: placement-fee row + receipt rows): partial_split shipment with two 22.60 lines -> same-cost netting 32 (standard line alone 38; whole-shipment netting 29 not applicable) -> 32; carry_span (parameter; program and activation date on the enrollment row): Core, 52 months -> 6 months, the 2026-06-05 line carries 3 (standard zero span) -> 29; near-miss: the 2026-02-11 over-receipt of 5 is 7 whole months old; tolerance_units (parameter): no other shortage case in 6 months and 52 months -> 0 (standard 1) -> 25; near-miss: the 2025-11-20 shortage case is 10 months old; tolerance_share (parameter): 300 expected -> 0.01 = 3 (standard 0.02 = 6) -> 23.

7. FACTOR CARD - shortage approval (6 factors: 5 parameter, 1 method; standard result 10, gold 23): approval_share (parameter, cross standing): Top Rated -> 1.0 (standard 0.9) -> 20; inbound_verification_holdback (method): 0 denied and 3 approved reimbursement cases in 12 months after the damage decision -> waived (standard 1) -> 22; near-miss: the 2025-09-30 denial is 12 whole months old; inbound_compliance_holdback (parameter, cross standing): 8 points -> 3 (standard 1) -> 25; line_ceiling_share (parameter): FBN Core Program -> 0.10 x 300 = 30 (standard 0.05 -> 15) -> 15; inbound_approval_limit (parameter, cross selling): Basic Store -> 20 (standard 10) -> 15; inbound_limit_uplift (parameter): opened 25 days ago -> 5 (standard 0) -> 20. Gold 23 differs from the corrected claim 26.

8. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. All three writes have subject fulfill_reimbursement, governed by fulfill_reimbursement_terms. Window: the warehouse-damage approval declares its own overwrite of "A warehouse loss claim is filed no later than the warehouse loss claim window counted in calendar days from the inventory adjustment date." for damage cases, replaced by the damage claim span counted back from the handling date; in this world both covered adjustments (2026-08-14, 2026-09-01) also lie inside the 60-day base window both at filing (20 and 2 days before 2026-09-03) and at the handling date (56 and 38 days), so every reading of the window gives the same 26 starting units. Inbound window: the line was received 2026-08-28; the case was opened 2026-09-14 (17 days later, after the 15-day reconciliation wait) and is corrected on 2026-10-09 (42 days, inside the 60-day claim window); a line received 2026-09-25 would be too early at handling, one received 2026-08-09 one day past it. Dedup gate inherited: no inbound-shortage reimbursement exists on NLIB-6402219 / WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR and the only damage reimbursement of the SKU settles the 2026-02-15 adjustment; each write binds reimbursement_type / object reference / sku to its case record. The shortage-claim policy overwrites the base shortage definition (netting and carry-forward); both approvals overwrite "Northloop reimburses units lost or damaged in its custody."

9. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Objects: the open inbound-shortage case (NLIB-6402219, WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR) and the open SKU-level warehouse-damage case (WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR). Rows included: the three lines of NLIB-6402219 (two netted by cost), the SKU's other receipts within 6 months, its damage adjustments, the seller's reimbursement cases opened within 6 and 12 months. Excluded by key: the lantern line (different cost), the carbon-pole and lantern history, the settled 2026-02-15 damage, the denied case outside 12 months.

10. CROSS-CATEGORY ROWS (charter consistency). Standing: Top Rated Level from the 2026-09-20 evaluation (evaluation day 20; next 2026-10-20); one intellectual_property violation recorded after that evaluation adds 8 points, which reaches the warning threshold of 8 and places the good-standing seller at risk for violation points; 8 is below the suspension threshold of 16, and the level stays until the next evaluation. Selling plan: Basic Store on an annual term from 2026-03-10, billed monthly on the 10th (next 2026-10-10). No payments account is seeded; no computation of this tree reads payout.

11. PERSONA DESIGN. Ignatius Marrowby, chatty, relies on his warehouse manager. Volunteers: the email, the short August shipment of SKU WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR, the claim filed September 14 for 38, wants it decided now by the agent. Only when asked: card last four 5147 and ZIP 98122; no shipment number at hand. Passive: lets the agent decide another claim first if told; makes the unit change himself with the agent's number when it is handed over; accepts the approved count and ends. He never mentions the damage claim or a wrong count.

12. STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate by email; verify with card + ZIP; read enrollment, cases, FBN activity, selling plan, standing; approve the damage case for 22; hand the seller the correction to 26; approve the shortage case for 23.

13. VERIFICATION. The scratch authoring script (deleted) replays gold with the real tools and evaluates each policy with check_compute's evaluator at its handling time: damage approval 22 (baselines 23/21/23/11/20, all-baseline 8); claim correction 26 (32/29/25/23, all-baseline 31); shortage approval 23 (20/22/25/15/15/20, all-baseline 10); skipping the damage approval -> 22, skipping the correction -> 25, swapping the two prerequisites -> 23.

14. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. The shortage approval rule names two waits; the case list shows an earlier submitted damage case on the same SKU and a shortage claim of 38; the damage rule gives min(26 claimed, 26 inside the claim span) - 1 - 3 = 22 (cap 23); the shortage-claim rule gives 32 - 3 - 3 = 26; after both, the approval rule gives floor((26 - 0 - 3) x 1.0) = 23 against caps 30 and 25. Same objects, order class and numbers as gold.

15. GATE RUNS (round 2, difficulty-wide block): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (13 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, closure 24 rows = initial_state); SOLVABILITY OK (3 calls, 3 base gates, 16 seed rows); COMPUTE OK (3 computations, 15 factors, 6 cross-difficulty, 16 history rows, 46 branches; suite means branches 40.00, steps 12.00; history max 24; branch max 46); GROUNDING OK; CACHE-DIFF INFO; SCOPE OK. check_traceability deferred to the KB render step.

16. REVISION LOG.
Round 1: the standing record and claim figures were retuned so gold differs from the corrected claim; the seller was renamed after a name collision with a sibling difficulty.
Round 2 (policy-task audit, item by item):
- F1 / T1-1 (warehouse-loss window superseded only for lost claims; damage approval ignored it): the damage approval now declares an overwrite of that window sentence with the damage claim span and starts from the claimed units limited to the damage adjustments inside the span. World: the damage adjustments moved to 2026-08-14 (10) and 2026-09-01 (16), the damage case to 2026-09-03 with 26 units, and an earlier 2026-02-15 damage (5 units, reimbursed automatically 2026-03-17) was added as a near-miss; the 102-day-late filing no longer exists, so readings A, B and C all give 22.
- T1-2 (standing row 7 points / at risk unreachable under the standing charter): the row is now 8 points from one intellectual_property violation recorded after the 2026-09-20 evaluation, at risk for violation points (warning threshold 8, suspension 16), evaluation dates on day 20.
- O-T1-a (shortage case filed 8 days after receipt, before the 15-day wait): the case now opens 2026-09-14, 17 days after receipt; the persona says September 14.
- O-T1-d (annual term next billing 2027-03-10): set to 2026-10-10 (monthly billing on the term-start day).
- O-T1-e (carry_span called multi-source): card 6 now states both conditions sit on the enrollment row; the task's multi-source factors are netting_scope and damage_allowance_method.
- O3 (denied/approved counts unfiltered): the counts filter case_type reimbursement_claim and the rule says "reimbursement case". O1 (naming): the order and baseline sentences now say "inbound verification holdback"; the line approval ceiling is stated as the line ceiling share of units expected with the standard share as the default. O5 docstrings reworded.
- No change, with evidence: O4 (the restated inbound correction window is an eligibility gate, not a quantity; it holds here: 42 days inside [15, 60]); O6 / O-T1-b (oldest-first decisions per SKU are the desk's rule for keeping each decision's case-history inputs settled; the edge's only effect is through the verification holdback, which that rule's own ladder reads); O7 / O-T1-c (missed automatic reimbursements are what the base parameter text calls "a reimbursement not issued automatically", and they are what the open damage case claims).
user_scenario:
You are Ignatius Marrowby, who runs Marrowby Trail Outfitters Co., a camping and hiking brand that stores its stock with Fulfilled by Northloop. You are friendly, a bit chatty and not very technical about Northloop's systems; you mostly go by what your warehouse manager tells you. Your problem: the inbound shipment you sent in late August arrived short on your trekking poles, SKU WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR. Your manager filed a shortage claim for it on September 14, putting in 38 units because that is how many fewer poles were counted than were on the shipment plan, and you have heard nothing since. You want that shortage claim decided today, and you are fine with the agent approving it from Northloop's side during this call.

To find your account you start with your email, ignatius.marrowby@marrowbytrail.com. You give the last four digits of your card on file, 5147, and your billing ZIP code, 98122, only when the agent asks you to verify who you are. If asked for the shipment number you say you don't have it handy but it was the shipment received at the end of August; if asked which product, you give WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR. If the agent asks about your store subscription or your seller rating, you say those are all on the account.

If the agent tells you that some other claim on your account has to be decided first, you tell them to go ahead and take care of it. If the agent explains that the unit count on your shortage claim has to be changed before it can be decided and asks you to change it yourself, you agree, and when the agent hands the change over to you, you enter exactly the number the agent gives you; you assume the agent can see things your manager could not. Once that is done, you ask the agent to go ahead and decide the shortage claim. When the agent tells you how many units of the shortage claim were approved, you say that is fine, thank them and hang up. If the agent gives you a number without saying the shortage claim is actually approved, you ask whether it is approved now.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.units_claimed: 26. Claimable shortage of line NLIB-6402219 / WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR (received 2026-08-28, 300 expected, 262 received): the shipment went under partial_split and carries two lines with declared unit cost 22.60 (WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR and WOG-TREK-POLE-CARBON, 100 expected / 106 received), so the netted shortage is measured over those same-cost lines = (300 + 100) - (262 + 106) = 32; the lantern line (cost 14.90, 80 / 83) is not netted; carry span 6 months (FBN Core Program, active 52 months) -> the SKU's other line inside it, 2026-06-05 (200 / 203), carries forward 3 (the 2026-02-11 over-receipt of 5 is 7 whole months old); tolerance units waived (no other inbound-shortage case opened in the 6-month case-history span, enrollment active at least 24 months); tolerance share 0.01 for a line of at least 200 units expected -> floor(300 x 0.01) = 3; no inbound-shortage reimbursement on the line; result 32 - 3 - 3 - 0 = 26. Baseline readings: line-alone shortage 38 -> 32; no carry -> 29; standard tolerance units 1 -> 25; standard share 0.02 -> 23.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.units_approved: 23. Units approved on the open inbound-shortage case at its handling time (after the damage case was approved and the claim corrected to 26): inbound verification holdback waived because none of the reimbursement cases opened inside the 12-month case-history span was denied and 3 were approved (2025-11-20, 2026-01-14 and the damage case of 2026-09-03 now approved; the denial of 2025-09-30 is 12 whole months old); high inbound compliance holdback 3 (8 active violation points); after holdbacks 26 - 0 - 3 = 23; approval share 1.0 for Top Rated Level -> 23; line ceiling floor(300 x 0.10 for FBN Core Program) = 30; inbound limit 20 (Basic Store) + uplift 5 (opened 25 days before, at least 14 but fewer than 30) = 25; result min(30, 25, 23) = 23. Baseline readings: standard share 0.9 -> 20; standard verification holdback 1 -> 22; standard compliance 1 -> 25; standard ceiling share 0.05 -> 15; standard limit 10 -> 15; no uplift -> 20.

edges.condition: The open inbound-shortage case carries, as its units claimed, the claimable shortage that the shortage-claim rule computes for its shipment line at handling time.
edges.policy_source: The units approved on an inbound shortage case are not fixed until the units claimed on that case equal the claimable shortage of its shipment line.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The open inbound-shortage case claims 38 units while the claimable shortage of line NLIB-6402219 / WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR is 26.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The seller's correction writes units_claimed = 26 on the shortage case, which stays submitted.

edges.condition: No damaged-in-warehouse case of the shortage case's SKU that was opened before the shortage case has case_status submitted; every such case stands decided.
edges.policy_source: An inbound shortage case is decided only after no warehouse-damage case of the same SKU opened before it still stands submitted.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The warehouse-damage case of WOG-TREK-POLE-PAIR opened 2026-09-03, before the shortage case of 2026-09-14, still stands submitted.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The desk approves the damage case for 22 units (case_status approved), so no earlier damage case of the SKU is submitted and the approved reimbursement-case count inside 12 months rises from 2 to 3.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisite writes touch different cases (the damage case and the shortage case) and neither policy reads the other's case: the damage approval reads only the damage case and the SKU's damage adjustments and receipts, the shortage correction reads only the shortage line and the inbound-shortage case count. Replaying with the correction before the damage approval gives the same root result (23) and the same terminal rows, so the two orders are equivalent; both must precede the root by the two prerequisite sentences.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the correction inbound_claimed stays 38 and units_approved = MN(30, 25, 38 - 0 - 3) = 25 instead of 23.

Without the damage approval only 2 reimbursement cases are approved inside 12 months, the inbound verification holdback is the standard 1 unit and units_approved = 22 instead of 23; the damage case also stays submitted in the terminal state.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for the late-August trekking-pole shortage claim to be decided.
